title: Quarterly cloudless mosaic tiles
description:
Every tile of the Copernicus Sentinel-2 Global Mosaics (`S2MSI_L3__MCQ`) for 36 quarters, 2017 Q1 through 2025 Q4: 1,017,575 mosaic tiles, 4,070,300 Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs, 607.5 TB, counted from the transfer's own per-quarter completion markers on 2026-09-28.

Each tile is a 10008 x 10008 pixel square at 10 m, about 100 km on a side, in the UTM zone of its MGRS grid cell. Four bands publish as separate single-band COGs: blue (`B02`), green (`B03`), red (`B04`) and wide near-infrared (`B08`). Pixels are `int16` reflectance, nodata `-32768`, and a value becomes surface reflectance when multiplied by 0.0001. That scale is **not** written into the GeoTIFF, so a client that reads the raw band and does not apply it gets numbers around 1000 where it expected 0.1.

The compositing rule is what makes these usable as a basemap. For each pixel and band, the upstream algorithm takes every Level-2A observation in the quarter, drops the ones the Sentinel-2 scene classification layer marks as cloud, and outputs the **first quartile** of the remaining distribution rather than the mean or the median. Taking a low percentile suppresses residual haze and bright cloud that the classifier missed, because those errors are one-sided: they make a pixel brighter, never darker. A pixel with no valid observation in the quarter is left empty. See the [mosaic algorithm note](https://documentation.dataspace.copernicus.eu/Data/Others/Sentinel2_Mosaic_Algorithm.html) for the upstream description.

Keys are fully constructible, so no index lookup is needed to read a tile: `{year}/{Qn}/{MGRS}_{i}_{j}/{band}.tif` under the catalog root. The STAC item id is the upstream one, `Sentinel-2_mosaic_{YYYY}_Q{n}_{MGRS}_{i}_{j}`.

This is a **mirror**, byte-identical to the upstream product for the four bands it carries. It does not carry the upstream `observations.tif` band, the `userdata.json` metadata, or the zipped `Product` asset, so `item_assets` here lists four assets where the [upstream collection](https://stac.dataspace.copernicus.eu/v1/collections/sentinel-2-global-mosaics) lists seven. Upstream the product is behind a Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem account; here it is anonymous, over HTTPS, with range requests and permissive CORS.

The item index publishes as one GeoParquet per quarter under `quarter=YYYY.Qn/items.parquet`, sorted tile-major so one tile's 36-quarter history is a contiguous run. **The index is not published yet**: `table:row_count` is 0 and `partition:file_count` is 0 until the first backfill lands, and each quarter gains an `item` link as its partition is written. Until then, read the per-quarter transfer manifests at `manifest/manifest_{year}_{Qn}.parquet`, which the agent guide documents.

A note on the band metadata below: the `eo:center_wavelength` values match the upstream collection, but `eo:full_width_half_max` does not. The values published upstream for this product are wrong, so the bandwidths here come from the [Sentinel-2 mission documentation](https://sentinels.copernicus.eu/copernicus/sentinel-2) instead. This is the one place this mirror deliberately departs from its source, and the collection README records why.

thumbnail.title: Natural-colour mosaic, 31UFU_0_0, 2024 Q2
thumbnail.description: Rendered from the published B04, B03 and B02 COGs of tile 31UFU_0_0 for 2024 Q2, read at the 1251 x 1251 overview level, scaled by 0.0001 and stretched between the 2nd and 98th percentile of each band. The Dutch coast, the IJsselmeer and the Afsluitdijk.

partition:keys.name: quarter
partition:keys.description: The mosaic quarter, written `YYYY.Qn`, for example `2024.Q2`. One `items.parquet` per quarter, sorted by `_tile`, then `datetime`, then `_subtile`, so one tile's whole history is a contiguous run and a tile lookup reads a small number of row groups. The `_subtile` tiebreak is what makes the order deterministic: `datetime` is constant inside a quarter file, and some MGRS cells carry more than one mosaic tile, so `_tile` and `datetime` alone leave those rows unordered. The dot rather than a hyphen keeps the value sorting in calendar order as a string. No partition file is published yet; each quarter gains its `item` link and its file as the backfill reaches it.

table:columns.name: id
table:columns.description: The upstream item id, `Sentinel-2_mosaic_{YYYY}_Q{n}_{MGRS}_{i}_{j}`. Unchanged from CDSE, so it joins straight against the source catalog.

table:columns.name: datetime
table:columns.description: The first instant of the quarter the mosaic composites, not an acquisition time. The compositing window is start_datetime to end_datetime.

table:columns.name: start_datetime
table:columns.description: First instant of the compositing window: the first day of the quarter.

table:columns.name: end_datetime
table:columns.description: Last instant of the compositing window: the end of the last day of the quarter.

table:columns.name: _tile
table:columns.description: The bare MGRS grid cell, for example `31UFU`. Join key against the coverage collection, and the first sort key. Query helper, not STAC.

table:columns.name: _subtile
table:columns.description: The full mosaic tile id, `{MGRS}_{i}_{j}`, for example `31UFU_0_0`. Unique within a quarter. Query helper, not STAC.

table:columns.name: _quarter
table:columns.description: The partition value, `YYYY.Qn`. Present in the row as well as the directory name, so a glob across quarters keeps it. Query helper, not STAC.

table:columns.name: grid:code
table:columns.description: The MGRS cell in STAC grid-extension form, `MGRS-31UFU`. The bare cell is `_tile`.

table:columns.name: proj:code
table:columns.description: The tile's own CRS as an authority code, for example `EPSG:32631`. Every tile is in its MGRS zone's UTM projection, not in EPSG:4326.

table:columns.name: proj:shape
table:columns.description: Raster shape in pixels, `[10008, 10008]` for every tile.

table:columns.name: proj:bbox
table:columns.description: The tile's bounding box in its own projected CRS, in metres: `[minx, miny, maxx, maxy]`, a 100,080 m square.

table:columns.name: gsd
table:columns.description: Ground sample distance in metres. Always 10.

table:columns.name: constellation
table:columns.description: Always `sentinel-2`. The mosaic composites observations from both Sentinel-2 satellites, so there is no single `platform`.

table:columns.name: instruments
table:columns.description: Always `["msi"]`.

table:columns.name: product:type
table:columns.description: Always `S2MSI_L3__MCQ`.

table:columns.name: processing:level
table:columns.description: Always `L3`. The mosaic is a Level-3 composite of Level-2A inputs.

table:columns.name: B02_href
table:columns.description: Full https URL of the blue COG. Promoted out of the assets JSON so a reader can open a band without parsing it.

table:columns.name: B03_href
table:columns.description: Full https URL of the green COG.

table:columns.name: B04_href
table:columns.description: Full https URL of the red COG.

table:columns.name: B08_href
table:columns.description: Full https URL of the near-infrared COG.

table:columns.name: assets
table:columns.description: The item's whole `assets` object as a JSON string, verbatim. Parse it with `json_extract` in DuckDB or `JSON.parse` in a browser. It carries `file:size`, `proj:transform` and `proj:shape` per band.

table:columns.name: links
table:columns.type: list<struct<href: string, rel: string, title: string, type: string>>
table:columns.description: The item's links, reduced to href, rel, title and type. `derived_from` points at the CDSE item this tile mirrors.

table:columns.name: collection
table:columns.description: Always `mosaics`.

table:columns.name: bbox
table:columns.description: The item bbox in EPSG:4326, `[west, south, east, north]`. A tile that crosses the antimeridian has `west > east`, per RFC 7946.

table:columns.name: geometry
table:columns.description: The tile footprint in EPSG:4326, as a Polygon, or a MultiPolygon split at 180 degrees for tiles that cross the antimeridian. Each edge is densified before reprojection, so it follows the true curve of the UTM square to under two metres.
